findings.title: Existing FGAPv2 realms never receive the new Clients resource type or scopes
findings.body: init() returns immediately whenever realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is non-null. Realms that enabled admin permissions before this change therefore keep only the Users all-resource resource and the old scope set; they never get the Clients all-resource resource or the new configure/map-roles-client-scope/map-roles-composite scopes. Creating a Clients scope permission in such a realm can fail while resolving scopes, and client permission evaluation that falls back to the Clients resource type has no resource to evaluate, so the new feature is broken for upgraded/existing realms rather than only for newly initialized ones.

findings.title: hasPermission can dereference a null all-clients resource
findings.body: When no resource exists for the specific client, the code loads the all-clients resource via AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource() and immediately passes it to policyStore.findByResource() and later calls resource.getScopes(). getResourceTypeResource() can return null (for example when the Clients all-resource resource is absent, as in realms initialized before this resource type existed). That turns a normal permission check into a NullPointerException/500 instead of returning false, potentially breaking client admin endpoints for the whole realm.

findings.title: setPermissionsEnabled now throws for callers reached through MgmtPermissionsV2
findings.body: MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() now always returns ClientPermissionsV2, whose setPermissionsEnabled() and isPermissionsEnabled() throw UnsupportedOperationException. Generic management callers still invoke these methods, notably AdminPermissions.registerListener() on ClientRemovedEvent/RoleRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent via AdminPermissions.management(), which selects MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever the V2 feature is enabled even though the listener only checks the V1 feature flag. If both FGAP features are enabled, deleting a client/role/group can fail with UnsupportedOperationException instead of performing the old cleanup/no-op, and other generic client-permission endpoints that probe isPermissionsEnabled() risk the same 500.

findings.title: getResourceName does not translate Clients resources
findings.body: getResourceName() only special-cases the Users resource type: it returns 'All users' for the all-users resource and resolves a user ID to a username, throwing if the user is missing. Clients resources fall through to resource.getDisplayName(). Resources created by getOrCreateResource() are created with the client ID as the resource name and no display name, and the all-clients resource is named 'Clients'. As a result, permission/resource representations for the new Clients type will expose a null/blank display name (or raw UUID) instead of 'All clients' or the client's clientId, unlike the Users behavior this feature mirrors.
